groups.title: Account
groups.intro: Sign the CLI in to your Tether account. The session is stored encrypted for your Windows user.

cmds.desc: Opens the web console in your browser; sign in and click Authorize CLI. With --email it signs in directly with a password instead.
opts: Sign in with email and password, without the browser.
cmds.keys: login sign in browser email password signup account

cmds.desc: Signs this computer out. Managed files stay on disk; nothing syncs until you sign in again.
Shows which account this computer is signed in as.

groups.title: Repositories
groups.intro: A repository holds the files and folders you share. Only you, the owner, see and manage it.

cmds.desc: Creates a repository.
Lists your repositories.
Lists what is in a repository with each item's share ID, version and artifact ID. Use it to find a share ID again.
cmds.keys: repo show share id artifacts repository

cmds.desc: Permanently deletes the repository and its history from the server. Everyone's copies stay on their disks but stop syncing.
Gives the repository to someone else. You stay on as an editor with delete permission.

Sets the line endings for files that match a pattern when they are first managed. Modes: auto, lf, crlf, binary, or unset to remove a rule. .sh files are always LF and .bat/.cmd CRLF unless a rule says otherwise.
cmds.keys: repo eol line endings crlf lf binary rule glob

groups.title: Share files
groups.intro: Upload a file or folder, then give people its share ID.

cmds.desc: Uploads a file or a whole folder into a repository and prints its share ID. You become the owner, and your copy is managed from then on.
opts: The repository to put it in (required).
For a path inside a git repository: keep, follow or skip. Without it you are asked. See Git repositories.
cmds.keys: manage upload share file folder owner eol git

cmds.desc: Gets a managed copy into the current folder (or dest). It never overwrites a different file that already exists, except a git-tracked file in keep mode, which git still has.
opts: keep, follow (editors) or skip, for a destination inside a git repository.
cmds.keys: pull get copy share id download git

cmds.desc: Adds a new file inside a managed folder, so everyone gets it. New files are otherwise ignored.

groups.title: Day to day
groups.intro: Managed copies undo local edits on their own. To change a file on purpose, start an edit and finish it with done. Commands that take a path also accept a folder and apply to everything managed inside it.

cmds.desc: Shows each managed file's mode, your role and version, and anything that needs attention: incoming versions, local changes, conflicts, files in use, live sessions and git state.
opts: Show every file in folders, with instance IDs.
cmds.keys: status modes pending conflict problems json

cmds.desc: Starts editing: your changes are kept until tether done, and incoming versions wait. If someone is editing the file live, you are warned to expect merge conflicts.
opts: Editors only. Every save is pushed to everyone within seconds, without done. One live editor per file; others are refused until you finish.

cmds.desc: Finishes editing: pushes your changes (only the changed parts travel) and asks what to do about conflicts, deleted files and files moved out of a folder. Without a path it uses the current folder.
opts: Answer every question with one choice: push, accept, keep-both, cancel, delete or stop. See choices.
cmds.keys: done finish push resolve conflict keep-both accept delete stop

cmds.desc: Stops syncing without forgetting the file: Tether still follows it through moves, but neither reverts nor updates it. Ends a live session too.
Resumes syncing unmanaged files and restores files deleted from a managed folder. If your copy differs from the shared one, you choose; nothing is pushed without asking.
Shows the difference between the server's current version and your copy.
Runs a sync pass now instead of waiting for the next one (every 30 seconds by default, every 3 seconds while a live session is involved).
Shows recent activity: reverts, updates, pushes with how many chunks travelled, followed moves, conflicts and notifications.
Shows the server's details for a file or folder: version, size, your role and, for owners, sharing settings.

groups.title: History & recovery
groups.intro: Every change is a version. Nothing is overwritten; a rollback adds a new version.

cmds.desc: Lists versions with who changed what and when.
Makes an earlier version current again for everyone. Also restores a deleted file.
Deletes for everyone. Copies stay on everyone's disk but stop syncing. The owner can restore it with rollback.
tags: Owner or editor with delete permission

cmds.desc: Re-links a copy Tether lost track of, for example after its drive was unplugged. Searches folders for matching content, or links a file you name. Instance IDs come from tether status -v.
opts: Link the only match without asking.

groups.title: Access
groups.intro: Owners decide who can change a file and who can pull it. People who pull with the share ID are viewers.

cmds.desc: With no option, shows the share ID, visibility, editors and allowlist. Each option makes one change.
opts: Make someone an editor (they can push changes).
With --editor: also allow deleting for everyone.
Turn an editor into a viewer. Their unpushed edits are reverted.
link (anyone with the share ID) or allowlist (only listed people).
Issue a new share ID. People who only had the old one lose access; editors and allowlisted people keep it.
cmds.keys: share editor viewer demote revoke allowlist visibility rotate id access permission can-delete

groups.title: Git repositories
groups.intro: When a managed file lives inside a git repository, manage and pull ask how Tether and git share it. Nothing is added to the repository.

cmds.desc: Shows or changes how managed files share their git repository.
opts: Tether's version wins. Git ignores Tether's copy, so git status stays clean and pulls are never blocked; git's changes to the file are undone.
Editors only. Whatever git puts in the file (pull, checkout, merge, rebase, reset, restore) is published to Tether. Teammates in follow mode get it through their own git pull.
cmds.keys: git keep follow mode repository pull checkout merge

groups.title: Background service
groups.intro: The tetherd service does the syncing. Any tether command starts it if it isn't running.

cmds.desc: Starts the background service.
Stops it. Files are not reverted or updated while it is stopped; moves are still found when it starts again.
Shows whether it is running and whether it starts at login.
Starts the service automatically when you log in to Windows (or with systemd --user on Linux).
Stops starting it at login.
Installs the latest tether-sync from npm and restarts the service. You are also told when an update is available.
opts: Only report whether an update is available.
cmds.note: Coming from 0.1.0, which has no update command? Run npm i -g tether-sync@latest once.

cmds.desc: Shows one setting or all of them.
Changes a setting.
cmds.keys: config set settings notifications tick server

settings: Web console for browser sign-in, if different from the server.
How long a vanished file may reappear before it counts as deleted (covers editors that save by replacing the file).
Folders searched for moved files on Linux, separated by commas.

modes.d: The default. The shared copy is the truth: if you change the file, Tether puts it back within seconds, and new versions arrive on their own.
You ran tether edit. Your changes are kept and nothing incoming overwrites them until you run tether done.
You ran tether unmanage. Tether still follows the file through moves and renames, but neither reverts nor updates it.
The file was deleted on the server or your access was removed. Your copy stays on disk but gets no more updates.
Tether can't find the file, for example after a drive was unplugged. Use tether locate to re-link it.

choices: Your version becomes current. Anything it replaces stays in history.
Take the server's version and discard your changes.
Save your copy as name (local copy).ext, then take the server's version.
Leave the file as it is for now.
Delete it for everyone (needs delete permission).
Stop managing it on this computer only.

s: Needs Node 22.13+. The browser opens: sign in and click Authorize CLI.
A repository holds the files you share.
Uploads it and prints a share ID. Your copy is managed from now on.
On another machine or account: an identical, managed copy.
Your changes are kept and incoming versions wait.
Save as often as you like.
Only the changed parts travel, and you are asked about any conflict.
Every save is pushed to everyone within seconds.
One live editor per file: others are refused until you finish.
Adds a new version that is the old one. Nothing is overwritten. Owner only.
keep: Tether wins and git ignores the copy. follow: git's changes are published to Tether.
Shows git state, conflicts and anything that needs attention.
